demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Domestic demand held firm, particularly in urban apparel, technical textiles, and home furnishings, while export growth remained constrained by soft demand in Europe and the United States and intensifying competition from lower-cost manufacturing bases
- Value-added garments, sustainable and recycled product categories, and man-made-fibre segments are the principal drivers of incremental demand
- Government interventions (PLI scheme, PM MITRA textile parks, RoDTEP remission) continue to support investment, capacity modernisation, and competitiveness across the value chain
- China+1 sourcing diversification by global buyers positions India, and mid-sized players such as the Company, as an increasingly attractive alternative destination
- Rising demand for organic cotton, recycled yarn, and environment-friendly processes opens avenues for higher-value, differentiated products
- Medium- to long-term outlook for the Indian textile sector remains constructive, supported by domestic demand, favourable policy measures, and global sourcing diversification, despite near-term headwinds from an uncertain global trade environment and competitive pricing pressures

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Company remains exposed to raw-material price volatility; cotton and other raw-material price volatility is flagged as a key structural concern affecting input costs.
- Company is exposed to foreign-exchange fluctuations on account of its export exposure.
- Evolving global trade and tariff policies, including possible tariff hikes in the United States, pose a direct risk to Indian textile exports, margins and sourcing preferences.
- Rising wage bills and aggressive pricing from competing manufacturing bases such as Bangladesh and Vietnam continue to compress margins.
- Elevated power and fuel costs remain a key structural concern for the industry and can materially affect input costs.
- A tight credit environment and delayed customer payments continue to strain working capital and cash flows; timely realisation of trade receivables continues to be an area of focused attention.
- A slowdown in key export markets, particularly Europe and the US, may continue to dampen export demand and realisations.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthen and diversify the customer base
- Invest selectively in sustainable and efficiency-enhancing technologies
- Continue to improve cost efficiency and product mix
- Reduce debt gradually and strengthen the balance sheet
- Transform into a future-ready textile player through operational excellence, customer centricity, technology adoption, and disciplined financial management
